requirements.text: The warehouse must record every vendor, a company from which goods are purchased.
A vendor is identified in business terms by its vendor account number.
The warehouse must retain both the vendor account number and the internal business entity identifier of each vendor, because other purchasing records point to the internal identifier.
requirements.obj: vendor account number and internal business entity identifier

requirements.text: The vendor's company name must be recorded and reportable.
Each vendor carries a credit rating on a five-point scale: Superior, Excellent, Above average, Average, Below average.
Reporting must present the vendor credit rating in its business wording, not as a bare code.
Each vendor carries a preferred vendor status, which is either 'preferred over other vendors supplying the same product' or 'do not use if another vendor is available'.
Purchasing management must be able to see whether orders are in fact being placed with preferred vendors.
Each vendor carries an active flag indicating whether the vendor is still actively used or is no longer used.
Vendors that are no longer used must remain in the warehouse so that historical orders placed with them stay reportable.
Where a vendor offers an electronic purchasing interface, the purchasing web service address must be recorded.
Reporting must tolerate the absence of the purchasing web service address, since it is not always populated.
The warehouse must retain the history of changes to vendor attributes, in particular credit rating, preferred status and active flag.
The state of a vendor at the time an order was placed must be reconstructable, not only its current state.
Whether the business needs the reason for a vendor credit rating or preferred-status change, and its source, must be confirmed with purchasing management.
The warehouse must record, for each combination of a product and a vendor, the standing commercial terms under which the product is bought from that vendor.
The same product may be supplied by several vendors, and a vendor may supply several products.
The supply relationship is identified in business terms by the pairing of the product and the vendor.
The average lead time, in days, between placing an order with the vendor and receiving the purchased product must be recorded for each product and vendor.
The standard price, the vendor's usual selling price for the product, must be recorded.
The last receipt cost, the selling price when the product was last purchased from the vendor, must be recorded.
The last receipt date, the date the product was last received from the vendor, must be recorded.
The business must be able to see price drift between the agreed standard price and the actually paid price.
The agreed minimum and maximum order quantities for the product from the vendor must be recorded so that buyers and reporting can see whether orders respect the agreed bounds.

Which minimum or maximum order quantity field carries which meaning must be confirmed with the purchasing team before either is used in reporting or threshold checks, because the source field descriptions are transposed.
The quantity currently on order for the product from the vendor must be available as an indicator of open commitment.
The unit of measure in which the product is bought from the vendor must be recorded.
Quantities and prices must always be interpreted together with the unit of measure, since the same product may be bought in different units from different vendors.
The warehouse must retain the history of supply term changes, such as price, lead time and quantity bounds, so that trends in agreed price and lead time per vendor and product can be analysed.
Reporting must be clear about whether it shows the current value or the value as at a point in time for running values such as quantity on order and last receipt figures.
The warehouse must be able to identify each purchased product consistently, even though products are maintained outside the purchasing area.
The warehouse must be able to join purchasing activity to the wider product information held elsewhere.
The warehouse must record every purchase order placed with a vendor.
A purchase order is identified in business terms by its purchase order number.
Each purchase order is placed with exactly one vendor.
Each purchase order is created by one employee, the buyer who raised it.
The warehouse must be able to report purchasing activity by the employee who created the order.
Employee name, department and role must come from the HR/employee area if the business wants to report on them, because only the identity of the creating employee is available in the purchasing area.
Each purchase order names a shipping method, the shipping company and rate agreement used to bring the goods to the business.
Each purchase order carries an order date, the date the order was created.
Each purchase order carries an estimated shipment date, the date the vendor is expected to ship.
The business must be able to compare the estimated shipment date against actual receipt activity.
requirements.obj: estimated shipment date against actual receipt

requirements.text: Each purchase order carries a status that is one of Pending, Approved, Rejected or Complete.
Reporting must present the purchase order status in business wording.
The business must be able to see the population of orders in each status, in particular orders that are approved but not yet complete.
Each purchase order carries a revision number, an incrementing counter tracking how the order has changed over time.
The business must be able to know whether an order was revised and how many times.
The warehouse must retain the history of a purchase order as it changes, including status transitions and revisions, rather than overwriting with the latest state.
The business must be able to answer when an order was approved and how long it sat pending.
requirements.obj: order approval time and pending duration

requirements.text: The business expectation on reconstructing full purchase order revision history must be agreed, since the source holds only the current version with its revision number and last-updated date and the outcome depends on source capture frequency.
Each purchase order carries a subtotal, the sum of the value of its lines.
Each purchase order carries a tax amount.
Each purchase order carries a freight (shipping cost) amount.
Each purchase order carries a total due to the vendor, equal to subtotal plus tax plus freight.
The business must be able to analyse purchasing spend by vendor, by employee, by shipping method, and over time, using order totals.
The warehouse must be able to demonstrate that the reported order totals are consistent with the underlying order lines.
Any discrepancy between the stated order total and the sum of its lines must be visible to the business as a finding.
Freight and tax are order-level charges and are not attributed to individual products in the source.
If product-level landed cost is wanted, the business must decide the basis for allocating freight and tax across order lines, as it cannot be derived from the source.
Each purchase order contains one or more lines, one per purchased product.
A purchase order line is identified in business terms by the purchase order it belongs to together with its line number.
Each purchase order line refers to exactly one product.
Each purchase order line carries the quantity ordered.
Each purchase order line carries the unit price, which is the vendor's selling price for a single unit of the product on this order.
Each purchase order line carries a line total, which is the ordered quantity multiplied by the unit price.
Each purchase order line carries a due date, the date on which the product is expected to be received, held per line so that different products on the same order may be expected at different times.
Delivery-performance analysis must work at line level, not only at order level.
The business must be able to compare the unit price actually paid on a line with the standard price agreed for that product and vendor, to identify off-contract purchasing.
requirements.obj: unit price paid versus standard price

requirements.text: Each purchase order line records the quantity actually received from the vendor.
Each purchase order line records the quantity rejected during inspection.
Each purchase order line records the quantity accepted into inventory, being the received quantity less the rejected quantity.
The business must be able to measure, per line, per order, per product and per vendor, the fulfilment gap between ordered and received quantities, including under-delivery and over-delivery.
The business must be able to measure inspection reject rates, being rejected quantity as a share of received quantity, by vendor and by product, as the primary indicator of incoming quality.

The warehouse must retain the progression of received and rejected quantities per line over the life of the order, so that the quantity received as at a given date can be answered and partial deliveries are visible.

The source records only cumulative received, rejected and accepted quantities per line with a last-updated date, and does not record individual receipt events, receipt dates or per-delivery inspection outcomes; analysis of individual deliveries requires another source or the requirement must be dropped.
The business must be able to compare the due date on a line against evidence of actual receipt in order to measure on-time delivery by vendor.
requirements.obj: line due date versus actual receipt

requirements.text: The practical measure of actual receipt timing currently available is the last receipt date on the vendor–product supply relationship, and its sufficiency for an on-time-delivery metric must be agreed with the business.

The business must be able to compare actual elapsed time from order to receipt against the average lead time recorded for that vendor and product, to validate whether recorded lead times are realistic.
requirements.obj: elapsed order-to-receipt time versus average lead time

requirements.text: The warehouse must record every shipping method available for inbound purchases.
A shipping method is identified in business terms by the shipping company name.
A shipping method has an internal shipping method identifier that is used on purchase orders.
Each shipping method carries a minimum shipping charge (ship base) and a charge per pound (ship rate), which are the terms on which freight is expected to be charged.
The business must be able to analyse freight cost by shipping method.
The business must be able to compare the freight actually charged on orders against the base and per-pound rates agreed with the shipping company.
The warehouse must retain the history of ship base and ship rate so that freight charged on a historical order can be assessed against the rates in force at that time.
requirements.obj: ship base and ship rate history

requirements.text: The technical replication identifier on shipping method records in the source has no business meaning and is not required for reporting.
A vendor supplies one or more products, and a product may be supplied by more than one vendor.
Each vendor–product supply relationship carries its own agreed price, lead time and order quantity bounds.
A purchase order is placed with exactly one vendor.
A purchase order is created by one employee.
A purchase order specifies one shipping method.
Receipt and inspection outcomes attach to the purchase order line, not to the order as a whole.

Products on order lines are normally but not necessarily products with a recorded supply relationship with that vendor; lines naming a product with no supply relationship for that vendor must be surfaced as a finding rather than hidden as a data error.
Every record in the purchasing source carries a last-modified date and time, which the warehouse must use to establish when information changed.
The warehouse must not present a value as current when a more recent change exists.

All monetary amounts in the purchasing area are held in a single currency in the source with no currency indicator; if vendors in other currencies are used, the currency of purchase orders and prices must be clarified.
Codes with defined business meanings, namely purchase order status, vendor credit rating, preferred vendor status and active flag, must be presented in reporting in their business wording.
The mapping of codes to business wording must be held once and applied consistently.
Quantities must always be interpreted together with the unit of measure recorded on the relevant vendor–product supply relationship.
Reporting must prevent aggregation of quantities across products or across units of measure without regard to the unit.
requirements.obj: aggregation of quantities across units of measure

requirements.text: Records that no longer represent current operational reality, such as inactive vendors, completed or rejected orders and discontinued supply relationships, must be retained in full.
Nothing may be physically removed because it has ceased to be current.

business_keys.rationale: REQ-002 explicitly states a vendor is identified in business terms by its vendor account number; it is business-recognised and retained per REQ-003. Source column Vendor.AccountNumber.

REQ-003 says other purchasing records (e.g. PurchaseOrderHeader.VendorID, ProductVendor.BusinessEntityID) point to this internal identifier, so it is needed for referencing, but it is system-assigned and weaker than the account number as a business key (REQ-002).
REQ-034 states a purchase order is identified in business terms by its purchase order number; it is unique and stable and is referenced by order lines (REQ-002-2).

business_keys.field: PurchaseOrderID + PurchaseOrderDetailID (purchase order with line number)
business_keys.rationale: REQ-002-2 states a line is identified by the purchase order it belongs to together with its line number; the composite is unique and not nullable.

REQ-031 and REQ-032 require consistent identification of purchased products maintained outside purchasing; REQ-003-2 and REQ-018 reference products on lines and supply relationships. ProductID appears in ProductVendor and PurchaseOrderDetail, but the requirements do not explicitly call it the unique identifier.
REQ-018 states the supply relationship is identified in business terms by the pairing of product and vendor (REQ-017, REQ-028-2). Source columns ProductVendor.ProductID and BusinessEntityID.
REQ-021-2 states a shipping method is identified in business terms by the shipping company name. Source column ShipMethod.Name.
REQ-022-2 notes this internal identifier is used on purchase orders (REQ-032), so it is needed for referencing, but it is system-generated and less preferred than the name (REQ-021-2).

REQ-036 and REQ-038 say only the identity of the creating employee is available in purchasing, with the rest held in HR. PurchaseOrderHeader.EmployeeID is the reference, but the requirements do not call it a business key explicitly.

# Generated Data Vault project (vault-agent)

A runnable dbt project: `models/staging/` computes the hash keys / hashdiffs via
AutomateDV's `stage` macro, `models/raw_vault/` holds the generated hubs, links, and
satellites. Review `review-queue.md` and `contracts/` before agreeing the model.

## Provide the raw inputs

Each staging model reads one raw relation by name — provide it either as a dbt seed
(`seeds/<name>.csv`, headers exactly as listed) or as a table/view in the target schema:

- `BusinessEntity` → feeds `stg_business_entity_businessentity` (expected columns: BUSINESSENTITYID, MODIFIEDDATE, LOAD_DATETIME, RECORD_SOURCE)
- `Person` → feeds `stg_business_entity_person` (expected columns: BUSINESSENTITYID, PERSONTYPE, NAMESTYLE, TITLE, FIRSTNAME, MIDDLENAME, LASTNAME, SUFFIX, MODIFIEDDATE, EMAILPROMOTION, ADDITIONALCONTACTINFO, DEMOGRAPHICS, LOAD_DATETIME, RECORD_SOURCE)

# ADR-0001: Data Vault model derived from requirements

**Status:** Proposed
**Date:** 2026-11-15
**Decision makers:** Vault-Agent (generated) — pending human review

## Context

This model was derived automatically by the Vault-Agent pipeline from 102 requirement(s) and 9 business key candidate(s). It records the Data Vault 2.0 structures the modeler chose and traces each back to the requirements that justify it.

## Decision

Model the following Data Vault 2.0 structures.

### Hubs (3)

- **hub_purchase_order** — business key `PurchaseOrderID`. A purchase order placed with a vendor, identified by its purchase order number. _(requirements: REQ-033, REQ-034, REQ-042-2)_
- **hub_purchase_order_line** — business key `purchase_order_line`. A purchase order line, identified by its purchase order together with its line number. _(requirements: REQ-001-2, REQ-002-2, REQ-008-2, REQ-033-2)_
- **hub_ship_method** — business key `Name`. A shipping method (shipping company and rate agreement) for inbound purchases, identified by the shipping company name. _(requirements: REQ-020-2, REQ-021-2, REQ-022-2, REQ-039)_

### Links (6)

- **link_product_vendor** — connects hub_product, hub_business_entity (vendor), hub_unit_measure. Product-vendor supply relationship from ProductVendor: a product bought from a vendor in a given unit of measure. Unit of work: ProductID + BusinessEntityID (vendor) with UnitMeasureCode of the supply terms. _(requirements: REQ-016, REQ-017, REQ-018, REQ-027, REQ-028, REQ-028-2, REQ-029-2, REQ-031, REQ-032, REQ-040-2)_
- **link_purchase_order_vendor** — connects hub_purchase_order, hub_business_entity (vendor). The vendor a purchase order is placed with (PurchaseOrderHeader.VendorID). Unit of work: PurchaseOrderID + VendorID. _(requirements: REQ-035, REQ-030-2, REQ-008, REQ-014, REQ-055)_
- **link_purchase_order_employee** — connects hub_purchase_order, hub_business_entity (employee). The employee (buyer) who created the purchase order (PurchaseOrderHeader.EmployeeID). Unit of work: PurchaseOrderID + EmployeeID. _(requirements: REQ-036, REQ-031-2, REQ-037, REQ-038, REQ-055)_
- **link_purchase_order_ship_method** — connects hub_purchase_order, hub_ship_method. The shipping method specified on a purchase order (PurchaseOrderHeader.ShipMethodID). Unit of work: PurchaseOrderID + ShipMethodID. _(requirements: REQ-039, REQ-032-2, REQ-024-2, REQ-025-2, REQ-055)_
- **link_purchase_order_line** — connects hub_purchase_order_line, hub_purchase_order, hub_product. A purchase order line belonging to its purchase order and referring to exactly one product (PurchaseOrderDetail). Unit of work: PurchaseOrderID + PurchaseOrderDetailID + ProductID. _(requirements: REQ-001-2, REQ-002-2, REQ-003-2, REQ-013-2, REQ-014-2, REQ-034-2, REQ-031, REQ-032)_
- **link_purchase_order_line_product** — connects hub_purchase_order_line, hub_product. Declared foreign key PurchaseOrderDetail.ProductID references PRODUCTNUMBER; ratified from the source catalogue (WP34). _(requirements: —)_

### Satellites (9)

- **sat_business_entity_vendor_details** — on hub_business_entity; payload: AccountNumber, Name, PurchasingWebServiceURL. Vendor identifying and descriptive attributes: vendor account number, company name and optional purchasing web service address. Source table: Vendor. Split rationale: Slowly changing identity/description of the vendor, separated from the status codes that change more often.. _(requirements: REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-011, REQ-012)_
- **sat_business_entity_vendor_status** — on hub_business_entity; payload: CreditRating, PreferredVendorStatus, ActiveFlag, ModifiedDate. Vendor status codes with history: credit rating, preferred vendor status and active flag. Source table: Vendor. Split rationale: Status codes change at a different rate and need tracked history; carries the vendor ModifiedDate once.. _(requirements: REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-009, REQ-010, REQ-013, REQ-014, REQ-035-2, REQ-038-2)_
- **sat_product_vendor_terms** — on link_product_vendor; payload: AverageLeadTime, StandardPrice, MinOrderQty, MaxOrderQty, ModifiedDate. Agreed standing supply terms per product and vendor: lead time, standard price and order quantity bounds. Source table: ProductVendor. Split rationale: Agreed contractual terms change rarely; split from operational running values.. _(requirements: REQ-019, REQ-020, REQ-023, REQ-024, REQ-025, REQ-029, REQ-029-2, REQ-009-2, REQ-019-2, REQ-035-2)_
- **sat_product_vendor_receipts** — on link_product_vendor; payload: LastReceiptCost, LastReceiptDate, OnOrderQty. Running operational values on the supply relationship: last receipt cost and date, and quantity currently on order. Source table: ProductVendor. Split rationale: Running values change with every receipt/order, far faster than the agreed terms.. _(requirements: REQ-021, REQ-022, REQ-023, REQ-026, REQ-030, REQ-018-2)_
- **sat_purchase_order_details** — on hub_purchase_order; payload: RevisionNumber, Status, OrderDate, ShipDate, ModifiedDate. Purchase order header state with history: revision number, status, order date and estimated shipment date. Source table: PurchaseOrderHeader. Split rationale: Lifecycle/status attributes tracked for status transitions and revisions.. _(requirements: REQ-040, REQ-041, REQ-042, REQ-043, REQ-044, REQ-045, REQ-046, REQ-047, REQ-048, REQ-049, REQ-050, REQ-035-2)_
- **sat_purchase_order_amounts** — on hub_purchase_order; payload: SubTotal, TaxAmt, Freight, TotalDue. Purchase order monetary amounts: subtotal, tax, freight and total due. Source table: PurchaseOrderHeader. Split rationale: Monetary amounts (different data type/concern) separated from lifecycle status.. _(requirements: REQ-051, REQ-052, REQ-053, REQ-054, REQ-055, REQ-056, REQ-057, REQ-058, REQ-025-2, REQ-037-2)_
- **sat_purchase_order_line_details** — on hub_purchase_order_line; payload: DueDate, OrderQty, UnitPrice, LineTotal, ModifiedDate. Ordered terms of a purchase order line: due date, ordered quantity, unit price and line total. Source table: PurchaseOrderDetail. Split rationale: Order terms set at ordering, rarely changing; split from receipt progression.. _(requirements: REQ-004-2, REQ-005-2, REQ-006-2, REQ-007-2, REQ-008-2, REQ-009-2, REQ-017-2, REQ-035-2)_
- **sat_purchase_order_line_receipt** — on hub_purchase_order_line; payload: ReceivedQty, RejectedQty, StockedQty. Cumulative receipt and inspection outcomes per line: received, rejected and accepted (stocked) quantities, with history of progression. Source table: PurchaseOrderDetail. Split rationale: Receipt quantities change repeatedly over the order life; separate rate of change from ordered terms.. _(requirements: REQ-010-2, REQ-011-2, REQ-012-2, REQ-013-2, REQ-014-2, REQ-015-2, REQ-016-2, REQ-033-2)_
- **sat_ship_method_details** — on hub_ship_method; payload: ShipBase, ShipRate, ModifiedDate. Shipping method rate terms with history: minimum charge (ship base) and charge per pound (ship rate). rowguid excluded as it has no business meaning. Source table: ShipMethod. _(requirements: REQ-023-2, REQ-024-2, REQ-025-2, REQ-026-2, REQ-027-2)_
